svg.text: Diagram 3 of 4 — Cluster launch sequence on the trust-zone map (per cluster start)

The L1 → L2 → L3 launch flow drawn over the diagram-1 topology · launch is done BY the Workspace SA (control-plane-owned); the VMs RUN AS the Compute SA · the launched cluster dials home over the backend SCC relay (cluster-initiated, TCP 6666)
reaches the VPC via corp VPN /

g.text: crosses B1 · then B2 via plproxy wire
executor VMs in the service project ·
the VMs boot as the Compute SA —
No inbound path to the cluster exists —
the SCC relay is always cluster-initiated.

the cluster manager acts as it for L2 · networkUser on
the node subnet + compute perms in the service project
IDENTITY · the launcher — never the VMs' runtime identity
workspace app · cluster manager (acts as the Workspace
SA for L2) · job scheduler · Unity Catalog metastore —
metadata only; data never transits here
notebook state / query text encrypted with customer
IDENTITY · Databricks-managed; customers reach it only via PSC
L2 · GCE: launch VMs — as the Workspace SA
VMs boot Runtime + Photon — as Compute SA

Identity split: launch is done BY the Workspace SA (the cluster manager acts as it across B6); the VMs RUN AS the Compute SA — never the Workspace SA. The cluster reaching RUNNING proves the backend PSC path end-to-end (private DNS → backend endpoint → ngrok attachment → relay).

B1 = corp → perimeter · B2 = frontend endpoint → plproxy attachment · B3 = backend endpoint → ngrok attachment · B6 = control plane → GCE API. Once running, the cluster also uses the frontend endpoint for REST / UC metadata — flow F4 in diagram 4. Setup crossings (B4): diagram 2.
